proofs.proof_tex: Fix \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and put \(z_\alpha:=z_{1-\alpha/2}\). By def:cross-fitted-estimator, \(\widehat V\ge n^{-1}>0\), so division by \(\sqrt{\widehat V}\) is valid. Define \(Z_{n,P}:=\sqrt n(\widehat\theta-\theta)/\sqrt{\widehat V}\) and \(F_{n,P}(z):=P(Z_{n,P}\le z)\). By def:wald-interval,\[\{\theta\in\mathcal I_{n,\alpha}\}=\{-z_\alpha\le Z_{n,P}\le z_\alpha\}.\]Let \(F_{n,P}(y-) := \lim_{u\uparrow y}F_{n,P}(u)\), which exists because every distribution function is nondecreasing. Hence\[P\{-z_\alpha\le Z_{n,P}\le z_\alpha\}=F_{n,P}(z_\alpha)-F_{n,P}((-z_\alpha)-).\]Set \(\delta_n:=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_4}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}|F_{n,P}(z)-\Phi(z)|\). The third conclusion of thm:uniform-endpoint-efficiency gives \(\delta_n\to0\). For every \(P\in\mathcal P_4\), the definition of \(\delta_n\), followed by passage to the limit \(u\uparrow-z_\alpha\) and continuity of \(\Phi\), yields\[|F_{n,P}(z_\alpha)-\Phi(z_\alpha)|\le\delta_n,\qquad |F_{n,P}((-z_\alpha)-)-\Phi(-z_\alpha)|\le\delta_n.\]Therefore, by the triangle inequality,\[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_4}\left|P\{\theta\in\mathcal I_{n,\alpha}\}-\{\Phi(z_\alpha)-\Phi(-z_\alpha)\}\right|\le2\delta_n\to0.\]Finally, def:wald-interval defines \(z_\alpha=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\). Since \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the standard normal distribution function is continuous and symmetric, and thus \(\Phi(z_\alpha)=1-\alpha/2\) and \(\Phi(-z_\alpha)=\alpha/2\). Consequently \(\Phi(z_\alpha)-\Phi(-z_\alpha)=1-\alpha\), which proves the claimed uniform coverage.
